title: Ensure 'application pool identity' is configured for all application pools
description: Application Pool Identities are the actual users/authorities that will run the worker process - w3wp.exe. Assigning the correct user authority will help ensure that applications can function properly, while not giving overly permissive permissions on the system. These identities can further be used in ACLs to protect system content. It is recommended that each Application Pool run under a unique identity. Every application pool and the applicationPoolDefaults must use identityType ApplicationPoolIdentity. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 1.4 Ensure 'application pool identity' is configured for all application pools

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $bad = @(Get-ChildItem IIS:\AppPools | Where-Object { $_.processModel.identityType -ne 'ApplicationPoolIdentity' }) + @((Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.applicationHost/applicationPools/applicationPoolDefaults/processModel' -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST') | Where-Object { $_.identityType -ne 'ApplicationPoolIdentity' }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: Set-ItemProperty IIS:\AppPools\<pool> -Name processModel.identityType -Value ApplicationPoolIdentity (and set applicationPoolDefaults the same way).

title: Ensure transport layer security for 'basic authentication' is configured
description: Basic Authentication can pass credentials across the network in clear text. It is therefore imperative that the traffic between client and server be encrypted, especially in cases where the site is publicly accessible and is recommended that TLS be configured and required for any Site or Application using Basic Authentication. For every site with Basic authentication enabled, system.webServer/security/access sslFlags must include Ssl (Require SSL). PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 2.6 Ensure transport layer security for 'basic authentication' is configured

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $bad = @(Get-Website | Where-Object { $b = Get-WebConfiguration -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Location $_.Name -Filter 'system.webServer/security/authentication/basicAuthentication'; $s = Get-WebConfiguration -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Location $_.Name -Filter 'system.webServer/security/access'; $b.enabled -eq $true -and [string]$s.sslFlags -notmatch 'Ssl' }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure 'passwordFormat' is not set to clear
description: The <credentials> element of the <authentication> element allows optional definitions of name and password for IIS Manager User accounts within the configuration file. Forms based authentication also uses these elements to define the users. IIS Manager Users can use the administration interface to connect to sites and applications in which they've been granted authorization. Note ... forms credentials passwordFormat must not be Clear in the root web.config or any site. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 2.7 Ensure 'passwordFormat' is not set to clear

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/authentication/forms/credentials' -PSPath $_; [string]$c.passwordFormat -eq 'Clear' }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: Set-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST/<site>' -Filter system.web/authentication/forms/credentials -Name passwordFormat -Value SHA1 (and replace clear-text passwords with hashes)

title: Ensure Handler is not granted Write and Script/Execute
description: Handler mappings can be configured to give permissions to Read, Write, Script, or Execute depending on what the use is for - reading static content, uploading files, executing scripts, etc. It is recommended to grant a handler either Execute/Script or Write permissions, but not both. The server-level handlers accessPolicy must not contain Write together with Script or Execute. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated. CIS marks this recommendation Manual; the automated check implements its audit procedure.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 4.8 Ensure Handler is not granted Write and Script/Execute

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $p = [string](Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/handlers' -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST').accessPolicy; if ($p -match 'Write' -and $p -match 'Script|Execute') { 'noncompliant' } else { 'compliant' }

title: Ensure 'notListedIsapisAllowed' is set to false
description: The notListedIsapisAllowed attribute is a server-level setting that is located in the ApplicationHost.config file in the <isapiCgiRestriction> element of the <system.webServer> section under <security>. This element ensures that malicious users cannot copy unauthorized ISAPI binaries to the Web server and then run them. It is recommended that notListedIsapisAllowed be set to false. isapiCgiRestriction notListedIsapisAllowed must be false. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 4.9 Ensure 'notListedIsapisAllowed' is set to false

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/security/isapiCgiRestriction' -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST'; if ($c.notListedIsapisAllowed -eq $false) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure 'notListedCgisAllowed' is set to false
description: The notListedCgisAllowed attribute is a server-level setting that is located in the ApplicationHost.config file in the <isapiCgiRestriction> element of the <system.webServer> section under <security>. This element ensures that malicious users cannot copy unauthorized CGI binaries to the Web server and then run them. It is recommended that notListedCgisAllowed be set to false. isapiCgiRestriction notListedCgisAllowed must be false. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 4.10 Ensure 'notListedCgisAllowed' is set to false

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/security/isapiCgiRestriction' -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST'; if ($c.notListedCgisAllowed -eq $false) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure FTP requests are encrypted
description: FTP Publishing Service for IIS supports adding an SSL certificate to an FTP site. Using an SSL certificate with an FTP site is also known as FTP-S or FTP over Secure Socket Layers (SSL). FTP-S is an RFC standard (RFC 4217) where an SSL certificate is added to an FTP site and thereby making it possible to perform secure file transfers. siteDefaults FTP ssl controlChannelPolicy and dataChannelPolicy must both be SslRequire. Not applicable when the FTP service is not installed. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated. CIS marks this recommendation Manual; the automated check implements its audit procedure.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 6.1 Ensure FTP requests are encrypted

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.applicationHost/sites/siteDefaults/ftpServer/security/ssl' -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST'; if ([string]$c.controlChannelPolicy -eq 'SslRequire' -and [string]$c.dataChannelPolicy -eq 'SslRequire') { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: Set-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Filter system.applicationHost/sites/siteDefaults/ftpServer/security/ssl -Name controlChannelPolicy -Value SslRequire; same for dataChannelPolicy (and assign an SSL certificate)

title: Ensure SSLv2 is Disabled
description: The SSLv2 protocol is not considered cryptographically secure, therefore should be disabled. SCHANNEL\Protocols\SSL 2.0\Server and \Client must both have Enabled=0 and DisabledByDefault=1. Affects every SCHANNEL service; a reboot is required after changes. PowerShell 5.1; reads the registry (run elevated).
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 7.2 Ensure SSLv2 is Disabled

audit.command: $base = 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols'; $bad = @('Server', 'Client' | Where-Object { $p = Get-ItemProperty -Path "$base\SSL 2.0\$_" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $null -eq $p -or $p.Enabled -ne 0 -or $p.DisabledByDefault -ne 1 }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: For both Server and Client: New-Item 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\SSL 2.0\Server' -Force | Out-Null; New-ItemProperty -Path <key> -Name Enabled -Value 0 -PropertyType DWord -Force; New-ItemProperty -Path <key> -Name DisabledByDefault -Value 1 -PropertyType DWord -Force; then reboot.

title: Ensure SSLv3 is Disabled
description: The SSLv3 protocol is not considered cryptographically secure, therefore should be disabled. SCHANNEL\Protocols\SSL 3.0\Server and \Client must both have Enabled=0 and DisabledByDefault=1. Affects every SCHANNEL service; a reboot is required after changes. PowerShell 5.1; reads the registry (run elevated).
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 7.3 Ensure SSLv3 is Disabled

audit.command: $base = 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols'; $bad = @('Server', 'Client' | Where-Object { $p = Get-ItemProperty -Path "$base\SSL 3.0\$_" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $null -eq $p -or $p.Enabled -ne 0 -or $p.DisabledByDefault -ne 1 }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: For both Server and Client: New-Item 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\SSL 3.0\Server' -Force | Out-Null; New-ItemProperty -Path <key> -Name Enabled -Value 0 -PropertyType DWord -Force; New-ItemProperty -Path <key> -Name DisabledByDefault -Value 1 -PropertyType DWord -Force; then reboot.

SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.0\Server and \Client must both have Enabled=0 and DisabledByDefault=1. Affects every SCHANNEL service; a reboot is required after changes. PowerShell 5.1; reads the registry (run elevated).
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 7.4 Ensure TLS 1.0 is Disabled

audit.command: $base = 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols'; $bad = @('Server', 'Client' | Where-Object { $p = Get-ItemProperty -Path "$base\TLS 1.0\$_" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $null -eq $p -or $p.Enabled -ne 0 -or $p.DisabledByDefault -ne 1 }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: For both Server and Client: New-Item 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.0\Server' -Force | Out-Null; New-ItemProperty -Path <key> -Name Enabled -Value 0 -PropertyType DWord -Force; New-ItemProperty -Path <key> -Name DisabledByDefault -Value 1 -PropertyType DWord -Force; then reboot.

title: Ensure TLS 1.1 is Disabled
description: The TLS 1.1 protocol is not considered cryptographically secure, therefore should be disabled. SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.1\Server and \Client must both have Enabled=0 and DisabledByDefault=1. Affects every SCHANNEL service; a reboot is required after changes. PowerShell 5.1; reads the registry (run elevated).
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 7.5 Ensure TLS 1.1 is Disabled

audit.command: $base = 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols'; $bad = @('Server', 'Client' | Where-Object { $p = Get-ItemProperty -Path "$base\TLS 1.1\$_" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $null -eq $p -or $p.Enabled -ne 0 -or $p.DisabledByDefault -ne 1 }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure NULL Cipher Suites is Disabled
description: The NULL cipher does not provide data confidentiality or integrity, therefore it is recommended that the NULL cipher be disabled. SCHANNEL\Ciphers\NULL must exist with Enabled=0 (read via the .NET registry API because the key names contain "/"). PowerShell 5.1; reads the registry (run elevated).
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 7.7 Ensure NULL Cipher Suites is Disabled

audit.command: $c = 'SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Ciphers'; function Get-Cipher($n) { $k = [Microsoft.Win32.Registry]::LocalMachine.OpenSubKey("$c\$n"); $v = $null; if ($k) { $v = $k.GetValue('Enabled'); $k.Close() }; $v }; $bad = @('NULL' | Where-Object { $v = Get-Cipher $_; $null -eq $v -or [long]$v -ne 0 }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: ([Microsoft.Win32.Registry]::LocalMachine.CreateSubKey('SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Ciphers\NULL')).SetValue('Enabled', 0, 'DWord') for each listed cipher (PowerShell drive paths cannot contain '/'), then reboot.

title: Ensure DES Cipher Suites is Disabled
description: The DES Cipher Suite is considered a weak symmetric-key cipher, therefore it is recommended that it be disabled. SCHANNEL\Ciphers\DES 56/56 must exist with Enabled=0 (read via the .NET registry API because the key names contain "/"). PowerShell 5.1; reads the registry (run elevated).
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 7.8 Ensure DES Cipher Suites is Disabled

audit.command: $c = 'SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Ciphers'; function Get-Cipher($n) { $k = [Microsoft.Win32.Registry]::LocalMachine.OpenSubKey("$c\$n"); $v = $null; if ($k) { $v = $k.GetValue('Enabled'); $k.Close() }; $v }; $bad = @('DES 56/56' | Where-Object { $v = Get-Cipher $_; $null -eq $v -or [long]$v -ne 0 }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: ([Microsoft.Win32.Registry]::LocalMachine.CreateSubKey('SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Ciphers\DES 56/56')).SetValue('Enabled', 0, 'DWord') for each listed cipher (PowerShell drive paths cannot contain '/'), then reboot.

title: Ensure RC4 Cipher Suites is Disabled
description: The RC4 Cipher Suites are considered insecure, therefore should be disabled. Note: RC4 cipher enabled by default on Server 2012 and 2012 R2 is RC4 128/128. SCHANNEL\Ciphers\RC4 40/128, RC4 56/128, RC4 64/128, RC4 128/128 must exist with Enabled=0 (read via the .NET registry API because the key names contain "/"). PowerShell 5.1; reads the registry (run elevated).
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 7.9 Ensure RC4 Cipher Suites is Disabled

audit.command: $c = 'SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Ciphers'; function Get-Cipher($n) { $k = [Microsoft.Win32.Registry]::LocalMachine.OpenSubKey("$c\$n"); $v = $null; if ($k) { $v = $k.GetValue('Enabled'); $k.Close() }; $v }; $bad = @('RC4 40/128', 'RC4 56/128', 'RC4 64/128', 'RC4 128/128' | Where-Object { $v = Get-Cipher $_; $null -eq $v -or [long]$v -ne 0 }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: ([Microsoft.Win32.Registry]::LocalMachine.CreateSubKey('SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Ciphers\RC4 40/128')).SetValue('Enabled', 0, 'DWord') for each listed cipher (PowerShell drive paths cannot contain '/'), then reboot.

title: Ensure 'Web content' is on non-system partition
description: Web resources published through IIS are mapped via Virtual Directories to physical locations on disk. It is recommended to map all Virtual Directories to a non-system disk volume. Fails when any site or virtual directory physicalPath is on the system drive. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated. CIS marks this recommendation Manual; the automated check implements its audit procedure.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 1.1 Ensure 'Web content' is on non-system partition

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $sd = $env:SystemDrive; $bad = @(Get-Website | Where-Object { [Environment]::ExpandEnvironmentVariables($_.physicalPath) -like "$sd*" }) + @(Get-WebVirtualDirectory | Where-Object { [Environment]::ExpandEnvironmentVariables($_.physicalPath) -like "$sd*" }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: Move content to a non-system volume (e.g. D:\inetpub) and update each site/virtual directory: Set-ItemProperty IIS:\Sites\<site> -Name physicalPath -Value <path>.

title: Ensure 'Host headers' are on all sites
description: Host headers provide the ability to host multiple websites on the same IP address and port. It is recommended that host headers be configured for all sites. Note: Wildcard host headers are now supported. Every http binding must include a host name (IP:port:host); bindings such as *:80: fail. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 1.2 Ensure 'Host headers' are on all sites

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $bad = @(Get-WebBinding | Where-Object { $_.protocol -eq 'http' -and ($_.bindingInformation -split ':')[2] -eq '' }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure 'Directory browsing' is set to Disabled
description: Directory browsing allows the contents of a directory to be displayed upon request from a web client. If directory browsing is enabled for a directory in Internet Information Services, users receive a page that lists the contents of the directory when the following two conditions are met: 1. No specific file is requested in the URL 2. directoryBrowse enabled must be false at server level and for every site. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 1.3 Ensure 'Directory browsing' is set to Disabled

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/directoryBrowse' -PSPath $_; $c.enabled -ne $false }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: Set-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Filter system.webServer/directoryBrowse -Name enabled -Value False (and remove site-level overrides).

title: Ensure 'unique application pools' is set for sites
description: Application Pool Identities allows Application Pools to be run under unique accounts without the need to create and manage local or domain accounts. It is recommended that all Sites run under unique, dedicated Application Pools. Fails when two or more sites share the same application pool. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 1.5 Ensure 'unique application pools' is set for sites

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $bad = @(Get-Website | Group-Object applicationPool | Where-Object { $_.Count -gt 1 }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: Create a dedicated pool per site and assign it: Set-ItemProperty -Path 'IIS:\Sites\<site>' -Name applicationPool -Value <pool>.

title: Ensure 'application pool identity' is configured for anonymous user identity
description: To achieve isolation in IIS, application pools can be run as separate identities. IIS can be configured to automatically use the application pool identity if no anonymous user account is configured for a web site. This can greatly reduce the number of accounts needed for Web sites and make management of the accounts easier. It is recommended the Application Pool Identity be set as the Anonymous User Identity. Every enabled anonymousAuthentication section (server level and all locations) must have an empty userName so the application pool identity is used. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 1.6 Ensure 'application pool identity' is configured for anonymous user identity

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $bad = @(Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/security/authentication/anonymousAuthentication' -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Recurse | Where-Object { $_.enabled -eq $true -and -not [string]::IsNullOrEmpty($_.userName) }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure' WebDav' feature is disabled
description: WebDAV is an extension to the HTTP protocol which allows clients to create, move, and delete files and resources on the web server. Note: The WebDAV feature must be enabled for this functionality to be available in IIS. The Web-DAV-Publishing Windows feature must not be installed (ServerManager module). PowerShell 5.1; reads the registry (run elevated).
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 1.7 Ensure' WebDav' feature is disabled

audit.command: $f = Get-WindowsFeature -Name Web-DAV-Publishing -ErrorAction Stop; if (-not $f.Installed) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure 'global authorization rule' is set to restrict access
description: IIS introduced URL Authorization, which allows the addition of Authorization rules to the actual URL, instead of the underlying file system resource, as a way to protect it. Authorization rules can be configured at the server, web site, folder (including Virtual Directories), or file level. Manual review: the benchmark gives no reliable automated check for this control.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 2.1 Ensure 'global authorization rule' is set to restrict access

audit.command: Verify an authorization rule specifying no access to all users except the Administrators group: To verify using AppCmd.exe enter the following command: %systemroot%\system32\inetsrv\appcmd list config - section:system.webserver/security/authorization OR To verify using PowerShell enter the following command: Get-WebConfiguration -pspath 'IIS:\' -filter 'system.webServer/security/authorization' OR At the web site or application level, verify that the authorization rule configured has been applied: 1. Connect to Internet Information Services (IIS Manager) 2.

remediation.command: To configure URL Authorization at the server level using command line utilities: Enter the following command in AppCmd.exe to configure: %systemroot%\system32\inetsrv\appcmd set config - section:system.webServer/security/authorization /- "[users='*',roles='',verbs='']" %systemroot%\system32\inetsrv\appcmd set config - section:system.webServer/security/authorization /+"[accessType='Allow',roles='Administrators']" OR Enter the following command in PowerShell to configure: Remove-WebConfigurationProperty -pspath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -filter "system.webServer/security/authorization" -name "." -AtElement @{users='*';roles='';verbs=''} Add-WebConfigurationProperty -pspath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -filter "system.webServer/security/authorization" -name "." -value @{accessType='Allow';roles='Administrators'} OR To configure URL Authorization at the server level using IIS Manager: 1.

title: Ensure access to sensitive site features is restricted to authenticated principals only
description: IIS supports both challenge-based and login redirection-based authentication methods. Challenge-based authentication methods, such as Integrated Windows Authentication, require a client to respond correctly to a server-initiated challenge. A login redirection- based authentication method such as Forms Authentication relies on redirection to a login page to determine the identity of the principal. Manual review: the benchmark gives no reliable automated check for this control.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 2.2 Ensure access to sensitive site features is restricted to authenticated principals only

audit.command: To verify that the authentication module is enabled for a specific site, application, or content, browse to and open the web.config file pertaining to the content. Verify the configuration file now has a mode defined within the <authentication> tags. The example below shows that Forms Authentication is configured, cookies will always be used, and SSL is required: <system.web> <authentication> <forms cookieless="UseCookies" requireSSL="true" /> </authentication> </system.web> OR To verify using AppCmd.exe enter the following command ...

remediation.command: When configuring an authentication module for the first time, each mechanism must be completely configured before use. Enabling authentication can be performed by using the user interface (UI), running AppCmd.exe commands in a command-line window, editing configuration files directly, or by writing WMI scripts. To verify an authentication mechanism is in place for sensitive content using the IIS Manager GUI: 1. Open IIS Manager and navigate to level with sensitive content 2. In Features View, double-click Authentication 3. On the Authentication page, make sure an authentication module is enabled, while anonymous authentication is enabled (Forms Authentication can have anonymous as well) 4. If necessary, select the desired authentication module, then in the Actions pane, click Enable OR Enter the following command in AppCmd.exe to configure ...

title: Ensure 'forms authentication' require SSL
description: Forms-based authentication can pass credentials across the network in clear text. It is therefore imperative that the traffic between client and server be encrypted using SSL, especially in cases where the site is publicly accessible. It is recommended that communications with any portion of a site using Forms Authentication be encrypted using SSL. Wherever forms authentication is the mode (root web.config and each site), forms requireSSL must be true. Compliant when forms authentication is not used. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 2.3 Ensure 'forms authentication' require SSL

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { $a = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/authentication' -PSPath $_; $f = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/authentication/forms' -PSPath $_; [string]$a.mode -eq 'Forms' -and ($f.requireSSL -ne $true) }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure 'cookie protection mode' is configured for forms authentication
description: The cookie protection mode defines the protection Forms Authentication cookies will be given within a configured application. The four cookie protection modes that can be defined are: Encryption and validation - Specifies that the application use both data validation and encryption to help protect the cookie; this option uses the configured data validation algorithm (based on the machine key) and triple-DES ... Wherever forms authentication is used, forms protection must be All (encryption and validation). Compliant when forms authentication is not used. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 2.5 Ensure 'cookie protection mode' is configured for forms authentication

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { $a = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/authentication' -PSPath $_; $f = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/authentication/forms' -PSPath $_; [string]$a.mode -eq 'Forms' -and ([string]$f.protection -ne 'All') }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure 'deployment method retail' is set
description: The <deployment retail> switch is intended for use by production IIS servers. This switch is used to help applications run with the best possible performance and least possible security information leakages by disabling the application's ability to generate trace output on a page, disabling the ability to display detailed error messages to end users, and disabling the debug switch. machine.config must contain <deployment retail="true" />. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated. CIS marks this recommendation Manual; the automated check implements its audit procedure.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 3.1 Ensure 'deployment method retail' is set

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/deployment' -PSPath 'MACHINE'; if ($c.retail -eq $true) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: In %windir%\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\<version>\Config\machine.config add <deployment retail="true" /> inside <system.web> (also in the 32-bit Framework copy).

title: Ensure IIS HTTP detailed errors are hidden from displaying remotely
description: A Web site's error pages are often set to show detailed error information for troubleshooting purposes during testing or initial deployment. To prevent unauthorized users from viewing this privileged information, detailed error pages must not be seen by remote users. This setting can be modified in the errorMode attribute setting for a Web site's error pages. httpErrors errorMode must be DetailedLocalOnly or Custom at server level and for every site. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 3.4 Ensure IIS HTTP detailed errors are hidden from displaying remotely

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/httpErrors' -PSPath $_; [string]$c.errorMode -notin @('DetailedLocalOnly', 'Custom') }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure 'cookies' are set with HttpOnly attribute
description: The httpOnlyCookies attribute of the httpCookies node determines if IIS will set the HttpOnly flag on HTTP cookies it sets. The HttpOnly flag indicates to the user agent that the cookie must not be accessible by client-side script (i.e document.cookie). It is recommended that the httpOnlyCookies attribute be set to true. httpCookies httpOnlyCookies must be true in the root web.config and every site. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 3.7 Ensure 'cookies' are set with HttpOnly attribute

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/httpCookies' -PSPath $_; $c.httpOnlyCookies -ne $true }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: Add <httpCookies httpOnlyCookies="true" /> inside <system.web> of each application web.config.

title: Ensure 'MachineKey validation method - .Net 4.5' is configured
description: The machineKey element of the ASP.NET web.config specifies the algorithm and keys that ASP.NET will use for encryption. The Machine Key feature can be managed to specify hashing and encryption settings for application services such as view state, Forms authentication, membership and roles, and anonymous identification. The following validation methods are available ... The .NET 4.x root web.config machineKey validation must be HMACSHA256 (HMACSHA384/512 are also accepted as stronger). PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 3.9 Ensure 'MachineKey validation method - .Net 4.5' is configured

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/machineKey' -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT'; if ([string]$c.validation -in @('HMACSHA256', 'HMACSHA384', 'HMACSHA512')) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure global .NET trust level is configured
description: An application's trust level determines the permissions that are granted by the ASP.NET code access security (CAS) policy. CAS defines two trust categories: full trust and partial trust. An application that has full trust permissions may access all resource types on a server and perform privileged operations, while applications that run with partial trust have varying levels of operating permissions and access to ... The global .NET trust level (root web.config) must be Medium (Low and Minimal are stricter and also accepted); the default Full fails. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 3.10 Ensure global .NET trust level is configured

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/trust' -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT'; if ([string]$c.level -in @('Medium', 'Low', 'Minimal')) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure Double-Encoded requests will be rejected
description: This Request Filter feature prevents attacks that rely on double-encoded requests and applies if an attacker submits a double-encoded request to IIS. When the double- encoded requests filter is enabled, IIS will go through a two iteration process of normalizing the request. If the first normalization differs from the second, the request is rejected and the error code is logged as a 404.11. requestFiltering allowDoubleEscaping must be false at server level and for every site. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 4.5 Ensure Double-Encoded requests will be rejected

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/security/requestFiltering' -PSPath $_; $c.allowDoubleEscaping -ne $false }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure 'HTTP Trace Method' is disabled
description: The HTTP TRACE method returns the contents of client HTTP requests in the entity- body of the TRACE response. Attackers could leverage this behavior to access sensitive information, such as authentication data or cookies, contained in the HTTP headers of the request. One such way to mitigate this is by using the <verbs> element of the <requestFiltering> collection. A server-level request filtering verb rule must deny TRACE (allowed=false). PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated. CIS marks this recommendation Manual; the automated check implements its audit procedure.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 4.6 Ensure 'HTTP Trace Method' is disabled

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $t = @(Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/security/requestFiltering/verbs/add' -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' | Where-Object { $_.verb -eq 'TRACE' -and $_.allowed -eq $false }); if ($t.Count -gt 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure Unlisted File Extensions are not allowed
description: The FileExtensions Request Filter allows administrators to define specific extensions their web server(s) will allow and disallow. The property allowUnlisted will cover all other file extensions not explicitly allowed or denied. Often times, extensions such as .config, .bat, .exe, to name a few, should never be served. The AllowExtensions and DenyExtensions options are the UrlScan equivalents. requestFiltering fileExtensions allowUnlisted must be false at server level (then allow only required extensions). PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 4.7 Ensure Unlisted File Extensions are not allowed

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/security/requestFiltering/fileExtensions' -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST'; if ($c.allowUnlisted -eq $false) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: Set-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Filter system.webServer/security/requestFiltering/fileExtensions -Name allowUnlisted -Value False (after adding <add fileExtension='.aspx' allowed='true'/> etc. for required types)

title: Ensure 'Dynamic IP Address Restrictions' is enabled
description: Dynamic IP address filtering allows administrators to configure the server to block access for IPs that exceed the specified number of requests or request frequency. Note: Ensure that you receive the Forbidden page once the block has been enforced. Dynamic IP Address Restrictions denyByConcurrentRequests must be enabled at server level (fails when the IP and Domain Restrictions feature is not installed). Tune maxConcurrentRequests to your traffic. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated. CIS marks this recommendation Manual; the automated check implements its audit procedure.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 4.11 Ensure 'Dynamic IP Address Restrictions' is enabled

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/security/dynamicIpSecurity/denyByConcurrentRequests' -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -ErrorAction Stop; if ($c.enabled -eq $true) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: Set-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Filter system.webServer/security/dynamicIpSecurity/denyByConcurrentRequests -Name enabled -Value True; set maxConcurrentRequests as appropriate

title: Ensure Default IIS web log location is moved
description: IIS will log relatively detailed information on every request. These logs are usually the first item looked at in a security response and can be the most valuable. Malicious users are aware of this and will often try to remove evidence of their activities. It is recommended that the default location for IIS log files be changed to a restricted, non-system drive. The siteDefaults logFile directory and every site log directory must not be on the system drive (default %SystemDrive%\inetpub\logs\LogFiles). PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 5.1 Ensure Default IIS web log location is moved

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $sd = $env:SystemDrive; $dirs = @((Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.applicationHost/sites/siteDefaults/logFile' -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST').directory) + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { $_.logFile.directory }); $bad = @($dirs | Where-Object { $_ -and [Environment]::ExpandEnvironmentVariables($_) -like "$sd*" }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: Set-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Filter system.applicationHost/sites/siteDefaults/logFile -Name directory -Value 'D:\IISLogs' (a non-system volume with restricted ACLs)

title: Ensure Advanced IIS logging is enabled
description: IIS Advanced Logging is a module which provides flexibility in logging requests and client data. It provides controls that allow businesses to specify what fields are important, easily add additional fields, and provide policies pertaining to log file rollover and Request Filtering. Manual review: the benchmark gives no reliable automated check for this control.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 5.2 Ensure Advanced IIS logging is enabled

audit.command: Browse to the location of the Advanced Logs and verify .log files are being generated. Note that logs will be written to disk after a non-determined period of time. They can be written into their specified directory immediately if, in the Log Definition, the Publish real- time events and Write to disk options are selected.

remediation.command: IIS Advanced Logging can be configured for servers, Web sites, and directories in IIS Manager. To enable Advanced Logging using the UI: 1. Open Internet Information Services (IIS) Manager 2. Click the server in the Connections pane 3. Double-click the Logging icon on the Home page 4. Click Select Fields The fields that will be logged need to be configured using the Add or Edit Fields button. Note: There may be performance considerations depending on the extent of the configuration.

title: Ensure 'ETW Logging' is enabled
description: Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) is a Windows feature that allows Administrators to send logging information to another location. This information is then compiled on the server and can be queried. siteDefaults logFile logTargetW3C must include ETW (File,ETW = both log file and ETW event). PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated. CIS marks this recommendation Manual; the automated check implements its audit procedure.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 5.3 Ensure 'ETW Logging' is enabled

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.applicationHost/sites/siteDefaults/logFile' -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST'; if ([string]$c.logTargetW3C -match 'ETW') { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure FTP Logon attempt restrictions is enabled
description: FTP Logon attempt restrictions is a built-in network security feature to automatically block brute force FTP attacks. This can be used to mitigate a malicious client from attempting a brute-force attack on a discovered account, such as the local administrator account. FTP logon attempt restrictions (system.ftpServer/security/authentication/denyByFailure enabled) must be on. Not applicable when the FTP service is not installed. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated. CIS marks this recommendation Manual; the automated check implements its audit procedure.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 6.2 Ensure FTP Logon attempt restrictions is enabled

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.ftpServer/security/authentication/denyByFailure' -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST'; if ($c.enabled -eq $true) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: Set-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Filter system.ftpServer/security/authentication/denyByFailure -Name enabled -Value True (set maxFailure and entryExpiration as required)

title: Ensure TLS 1.2 is Enabled
description: TLS 1.2 is the most recent and mature protocol for protecting the confidentiality and integrity of HTTP traffic. SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.2\Server must have Enabled=1 and DisabledByDefault=0. PowerShell 5.1; reads the registry (run elevated).
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 7.6 Ensure TLS 1.2 is Enabled

audit.command: $base = 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols'; $p = Get-ItemProperty -Path "$base\TLS 1.2\Server" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if ($null -ne $p -and $p.Enabled -eq 1 -and $p.DisabledByDefault -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: New-Item 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.2\Server' -Force | Out-Null; set DWORD Enabled=1 and DisabledByDefault=0, then reboot.

title: Ensure AES 128/128 Cipher Suite is Disabled
description: The AES 128/128 Cipher Suite is not considered secure and therefore should be disabled, if possible. SCHANNEL\Ciphers\AES 128/128 must exist with Enabled=0 (read via the .NET registry API because the key names contain "/"). PowerShell 5.1; reads the registry (run elevated).
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 7.10 Ensure AES 128/128 Cipher Suite is Disabled

audit.command: $c = 'SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Ciphers'; function Get-Cipher($n) { $k = [Microsoft.Win32.Registry]::LocalMachine.OpenSubKey("$c\$n"); $v = $null; if ($k) { $v = $k.GetValue('Enabled'); $k.Close() }; $v }; $bad = @('AES 128/128' | Where-Object { $v = Get-Cipher $_; $null -eq $v -or [long]$v -ne 0 }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: ([Microsoft.Win32.Registry]::LocalMachine.CreateSubKey('SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Ciphers\AES 128/128')).SetValue('Enabled', 0, 'DWord') for each listed cipher (PowerShell drive paths cannot contain '/'), then reboot.

title: Ensure AES 256/256 Cipher Suite is Enabled
description: AES 256/256 is the most recent and mature cipher suite for protecting the confidentiality and integrity of HTTP traffic. Enabling AES 256/256 is recommended. Note: AES 256/256 is enabled by default starting with Server 2012 and 2012 R2. SCHANNEL\Ciphers\AES 256/256 must exist with Enabled=1 (read via the .NET registry API). PowerShell 5.1; reads the registry (run elevated).
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 7.11 Ensure AES 256/256 Cipher Suite is Enabled

audit.command: $c = 'SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Ciphers'; function Get-Cipher($n) { $k = [Microsoft.Win32.Registry]::LocalMachine.OpenSubKey("$c\$n"); $v = $null; if ($k) { $v = $k.GetValue('Enabled'); $k.Close() }; $v }; $v = Get-Cipher 'AES 256/256'; if ($null -ne $v -and [long]$v -eq 1) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure 'forms authentication' is set to use cookies
description: Forms Authentication can be configured to maintain the site visitor's session identifier in either a URI or cookie. It is recommended that Forms Authentication be set to use cookies. Wherever forms authentication is used, forms cookieless must be UseCookies. Compliant when forms authentication is not used. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 2.4 Ensure 'forms authentication' is set to use cookies

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { $a = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/authentication' -PSPath $_; $f = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/authentication/forms' -PSPath $_; [string]$a.mode -eq 'Forms' -and ([string]$f.cookieless -ne 'UseCookies') }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure 'credentials' are not stored in configuration files
description: The <credentials> element of the <authentication> element allows optional definitions of name and password for IIS Manager User accounts within the configuration file. Forms based authentication also uses these elements to define the users. IIS Manager Users can use the administration interface to connect to sites and applications in which they've been granted authorization. Note ... No forms credentials <user> entries may be stored in the root web.config or any site configuration. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 2.8 Ensure 'credentials' are not stored in configuration files

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { @(Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/authentication/forms/credentials/user' -PSPath $_).Count -gt 0 }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure 'debug' is turned off
description: Developers often enable the debug mode during active ASP.NET development so that they do not have to continually clear their browsers cache every time they make a change to a resource handler. The problem would arise from this being left "on" or set to "true". Compilation debug output is displayed to the end user, allowing malicious persons to obtain detailed information about applications. compilation debug must be false in the root web.config and every site. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 3.2 Ensure 'debug' is turned off

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/compilation' -PSPath $_; $c.debug -ne $false }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure custom error messages are not off
description: When an ASP.NET application fails and causes an HTTP/1.x 500 Internal Server Error, or a feature configuration (such as Request Filtering) prevents a page from being displayed, an error message will be generated. Administrators can choose whether or not the application should display a friendly message to the client, detailed error message to the client, or detailed error message to localhost only. customErrors mode must be RemoteOnly or On (not Off) in the root web.config and every site. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 3.3 Ensure custom error messages are not off

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/customErrors' -PSPath $_; [string]$c.mode -eq 'Off' }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure ASP.NET stack tracing is not enabled
description: The trace element configures the ASP.NET code tracing service that controls how trace results are gathered, stored, and displayed. When tracing is enabled, each page request generates trace messages that can be appended to the page output or stored in an application trace log. ASP.NET trace must not be enabled in the root web.config or any site (page-level Trace="true" is not checked). PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 3.5 Ensure ASP.NET stack tracing is not enabled

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/trace' -PSPath $_; $c.enabled -eq $true }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure 'httpcookie' mode is configured for session state
description: A session cookie associates session information with client information for that session, which can be the duration of a user's connection to a site. The cookie is passed in a HTTP header together with all requests between the client and server. Session information can also be stored in the URL. sessionState cookieless must be UseCookies in the root web.config and every site. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 3.6 Ensure 'httpcookie' mode is configured for session state

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.web/sessionState' -PSPath $_; [string]$c.cookieless -ne 'UseCookies' }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure 'MachineKey validation method - .Net 3.5' is configured
description: The machineKey element of the ASP.NET web.config specifies the algorithm and keys that ASP.NET will use for encryption. The Machine Key feature can be managed to specify hashing and encryption settings for application services such as view state, Forms authentication, membership and roles, and anonymous identification. The following validation methods are available ... Manual review: the benchmark gives no reliable automated check for this control.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 3.8 Ensure 'MachineKey validation method - .Net 3.5' is configured

audit.command: To verify the Machine Key validation method using IIS Manager: 1. Open IIS Manager and navigate to the level that was configured, the WEBROOT, or server in this case 2. In the features view, double click Machine Key 3. On the Machine Key page, verify that SHA1 is selected in the validation method dropdown

remediation.command: Machine key encryption can be set by using the UI, running appcmd.exe commands, by editing configuration files directly, or by writing WMI scripts. To set the Machine Key encryption at the global level using an appcmd.exe command: %systemroot%\system32\inetsrv\appcmd set config /commit:WEBROOT /section:machineKey /validation:SHA1 Note: When Appcmd.exe is used to configure the <machineKey> element at the global level in IIS, the /commit:WEBROOT switch must be included so that configuration changes are made to the root web.config file instead of ApplicationHost.config.

title: Ensure X-Powered-By Header is removed
description: The x-powered-by headers specify the underlying technology used by the webserver. No X-Powered-By custom header may be configured at server level or for any site. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated. CIS marks this recommendation Manual; the automated check implements its audit procedure.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 3.11 Ensure X-Powered-By Header is removed

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { @(Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/httpProtocol/customHeaders/add' -PSPath $_ | Where-Object { $_.name -eq 'X-Powered-By' }).Count -gt 0 }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure Server Header is removed
description: The server header headers specify the underlying technology used by the application. requestFiltering removeServerHeader must be true at server level (IIS 10 1709 or later). PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated. CIS marks this recommendation Manual; the automated check implements its audit procedure.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 3.12 Ensure Server Header is removed

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/security/requestFiltering' -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST'; if ($c.removeServerHeader -eq $true) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure 'maxAllowedContentLength' is configured
description: The maxAllowedContentLength Request Filter is the maximum size of the http request, measured in bytes, which can be sent from a client to the server. Configuring this value enables the total request size to be restricted to a configured value. It is recommended that the overall size of requests be restricted to a maximum value appropriate for the server, site, or application. Manual review: the benchmark gives no reliable automated check for this control.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 4.1 Ensure 'maxAllowedContentLength' is configured

audit.command: Upon exceeding the configured value set for the Request Filter, IIS will throw a Status Code 404.13. To manually verify the change, locate and open the web.config for the web site or application in which the request filter was set. Ensure the value defined for maxAllowedContentLength is what was set. The 28.6MB max example would show: <configuration> <system.webServer> <security> <requestFiltering> <requestLimits maxAllowedContentLength="30000000" /> </requestFiltering> </security> </system.webServer> </configuration> OR To verify using PowerShell enter the following command ...

remediation.command: The MaxAllowedContentLength Request Filter may be set for a server, website, or application using the IIS Manager GUI, using AppCmd.exe commands in a command-line window, and/or directly editing the configuration files. To configure using the IIS Manager GUI: 1. Open Internet Information Services (IIS) Manager 2. In the Connections pane, click on the server, site, application, or directory to be configured 3. In the Home pane, double-click Request Filtering 4. Click Edit Feature Settings... in the Actions pane 5. Under the Request Limits section, key the maximum content length in bytes that will allow applications to retain their intended functionality, such as 30000000 (approx. 28.6 MB) Enter the following command in AppCmd.exe to configure ...

title: Ensure 'maxURL request filter' is configured
description: The maxURL attribute of the <requestLimits> property is the maximum length (in Bytes) in which a requested URL can be (excluding query string) in order for IIS to accept. Configuring this Request Filter enables administrators to restrict the length of the requests that the server will accept. It is recommended that a limit be put on the length of URL. requestLimits maxUrl must be 4096 or lower at server level and for every site (default 4096). PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 4.2 Ensure 'maxURL request filter' is configured

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/security/requestFiltering/requestLimits' -PSPath $_; [long]$c.maxUrl -gt 4096 }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure 'MaxQueryString request filter' is configured
description: The MaxQueryString Request Filter describes the upper limit on the length of the query string that the configured IIS server will allow for websites or applications. It is recommended that values always be established to limit the amount of data that can be accepted in the query string. requestLimits maxQueryString must be 2048 or lower at server level and for every site (default 2048). PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 4.3 Ensure 'MaxQueryString request filter' is configured

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/security/requestFiltering/requestLimits' -PSPath $_; [long]$c.maxQueryString -gt 2048 }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure non-ASCII characters in URLs are not allowed
description: This feature is used to allow or reject all requests to IIS that contain non-ASCII characters. When using this feature, Request Filtering will deny the request if high-bit characters are present in the URL. The UrlScan equivalent is AllowHighBitCharacters. It is recommended that requests containing non-ASCII characters be rejected, where possible. requestFiltering allowHighBitCharacters must be false at server level and for every site. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 4.4 Ensure non-ASCII characters in URLs are not allowed

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; $paths = @('MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST') + @(Get-Website | ForEach-Object { "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" }); $bad = @($paths | Where-Object { $c = Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/security/requestFiltering' -PSPath $_; $c.allowHighBitCharacters -ne $false }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

title: Ensure HSTS Header is set
description: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) allows a site to inform the user agent to communicate with the site only over HTTPS. This header takes two parameters: max- age, "specifies the number of seconds, after the reception of the STS header field, during which the user agent regards the host (from whom the message was received) as a Known HSTS Host [speaks only HTTPS]"; and includeSubDomains. A Strict-Transport-Security custom header with max-age greater than 0 (480 or more recommended) must be set at server level or for every site. PowerShell 5.1 with the WebAdministration module; run elevated. CIS marks this recommendation Manual; the automated check implements its audit procedure.
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 7.1 Ensure HSTS Header is set

audit.command: Import-Module WebAdministration -ErrorAction Stop; function Test-Hsts($p) { @(Get-WebConfiguration -Filter 'system.webServer/httpProtocol/customHeaders/add' -PSPath $p | Where-Object { $_.name -eq 'Strict-Transport-Security' -and $_.value -match 'max-age=([0-9]+)' -and [long]$Matches[1] -gt 0 }).Count -gt 0 }; if (Test-Hsts 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST') { 'compliant' } else { $bad = @(Get-Website | Where-Object { -not (Test-Hsts "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)") }); if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' } }

title: Ensure TLS Cipher Suite ordering is Configured
description: Cipher suites are a named combination of authentication, encryption, message authentication code, and key exchange algorithms used for the security settings of a network connection using TLS protocol. Clients send a cipher list and a list of ciphers that it supports in order of preference to a server. The server then replies with the cipher suite that it selects from the client cipher suite list. HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Cryptography\Configuration\SSL\00010002 Functions must equal the benchmark cipher suite order: TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA384,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA384,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256. PowerShell 5.1; reads the registry (run elevated).
reference: CIS Microsoft IIS 10 Benchmark v1.2.1 - 7.12 Ensure TLS Cipher Suite ordering is Configured

audit.command: $p = Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Cryptography\Configuration\SSL\00010002' -Name Functions -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $v = if ($p) { (@($p.Functions) -join ',') -replace '\s', '' } else { '' }; if ($v -eq 'TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA384,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA384,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256') { 'compliant' } else { 'noncompliant' }

remediation.command: New-Item 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Cryptography\Configuration\SSL\00010002' -Force | Out-Null; New-ItemProperty -Path <that key> -Name Functions -Value 'TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA384,TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA384,TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256' -PropertyType String -Force (or GPO: SSL Cipher Suite Order), then reboot.
